goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

per_golden_matches.matched_candidate: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 — i.content is nil for RSS 2.0 feeds that only supply description, so .scrub raises NoMethodError and aborts the whole poll (retry: false)

This is the same underlying issue as the golden comment, including the need to handle feeds that only provide `description`.

This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/best.html.erb:6 — <%- end if %>` is a Ruby syntax error so the success template never renders, yet controller specs pass because render_views is off
spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:40 — Spec mocks TopicRetriever instead of asserting the enqueued RetrieveTopic payload, so wrong/missing job args pass silently

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when no `topic_id` is found it calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: current_user.try(:id), embed_url: embed_url)` and renders `loading`; it never instantiates or calls `TopicRetriever`. However, `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb` expects `TopicRetriever.new` and `retriever.retrieve` to be called. This means the spec is testing the wrong behavior (and would fail) and it also does not assert the enqueued job/payload that the controller actually uses.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:8 — "404 without an embed_url" only asserts `should_not be_success`, so an unhandled ParameterMissing 500 satisfies it

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best the line `embed_url = params.require(:embed_url)` will raise `ActionController::ParameterMissing` when `embed_url` is absent. The spec `it "is 404 without an embed_url" do get :best; response.should_not be_success end` only asserts non-success, so it would pass for a 400/500 response (or any error handled into a non-2xx response) and does not actually verify a 404 as the example description claims. This is a real weakness/mismatch in the newly added test in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:27 — setnx followed by a separate expire is non-atomic; a crash in between leaves a permanent throttle key and that embed_url is never retrieved again

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb `retrieved_recently?` uses `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and then, in a separate call, `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. These two operations are not atomic; if the process crashes or loses connectivity after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` is applied, the key will remain without a TTL. Subsequent calls will see `setnx` return false and treat the URL as “retrieved recently” forever, preventing `perform_retrieve` for that `embed_url` until the key is manually removed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:26 — Throttle key embeds the raw caller-supplied URL with no length bound or site namespace, allowing unbounded redis key growth

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, the Redis throttle key is constructed as `retrieved:#{@embed_url}` where `@embed_url` is caller-supplied. There is no normalization or length limit, so a client can supply a very long (but valid and host-matching) URL or many distinct URLs on the same host, causing many large Redis keys to be created. Although keys are set to expire after 60 seconds, this still allows potentially unbounded key size and high transient key cardinality/memory use under request flooding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb:34 — Every throttle test stubs `retrieved_recently?`, so the redis logic is never exercised and a completely broken throttle still passes

adjudication.rationale: In spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb (the two examples under "with a valid host"), both throttle-related tests explicitly stub `retrieved_recently?` to return true/false (`topic_retriever.expects(:retrieved_recently?).returns(false/true)`). That means the actual implementation of `retrieved_recently?` in lib/topic_retriever.rb (which contains the Redis `setnx`/`expire` throttle logic) is never executed by these specs. As a result, the tests would still pass even if the Redis throttle code were broken or removed, so the finding is verifiably accurate about the diff introducing unexercised throttle logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:37 — exists?-then-import is a TOCTOU race with the hourly PollFeed and other RetrieveTopic jobs, producing duplicate-key failures on the unique embed_url index

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In lib/topic_retriever.rb#perform_retrieve the code does `return if TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?` and later (after possibly running PollFeed) calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, which eventually calls `TopicEmbed.import`. In TopicEmbed.import it again does `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and, if blank, proceeds to `TopicEmbed.create!` under a unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url`. Two concurrent RetrieveTopic jobs (or PollFeed + RetrieveTopic) can both observe “no row”, both create, and the loser will raise a duplicate key/RecordNotUnique because there is no locking or rescue. That is a classic TOCTOU race leading to sporadic failures.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:15 — Read-then-create! race on embed_url raises RecordNotUnique inside the transaction, aborting the caller instead of resolving to the existing embed

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, it does `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and if blank enters a `Topic.transaction` and then calls `TopicEmbed.create!` with that same `embed_url`. The migration adds `add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true`. Under concurrent calls with the same URL, both can observe `embed.blank?` and both attempt `create!`; the second will hit the unique index and raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` inside the transaction. There is no rescue/retry or fallback to load the existing record, so the exception will propagate and abort the caller/job instead of resolving to the already-created embed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:31 — No per-item rescue: one malformed item raises and aborts the whole feed loop, so every later item is silently dropped for that run

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb the job does `rss.items.each do |i| ... content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub) ... end` with no per-item error handling. If any item has unexpected/missing fields (e.g., `i.content` is nil so `nil.scrub` raises, or `TopicEmbed.import` raises), the exception will abort the entire `poll_feed` run and later items won’t be processed. Because the job also sets `sidekiq_options retry: false`, that run’s remaining items are effectively dropped until the next schedule.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 — i.content` is nil for description-only RSS items, so `.scrub` raises NoMethodError on very common feeds
app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 — Kernel#open on a settings URL permits `|command` execution and SSRF, and has no timeout or size cap so a hostile feed can hang or OOM the worker
app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — import_remote opens a caller-supplied URL with no timeout/size limit and follows redirects, letting the embeddable host redirect into internal addresses

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` does `open(url).read` on the supplied `url` (from `TopicRetriever`, which ultimately comes from `params[:embed_url]` in `EmbedController#best`). While `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` restricts the *initial* URL host to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, `open-uri` will follow HTTP redirects by default and does not enforce that redirects stay on the same host. That means an allowed host could redirect to an internal/private address, enabling SSRF. Additionally, the code provides no explicit timeouts or response size limits when reading the remote body (`.read`), so it can hang or consume large memory on large/slow responses.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:131 — raw_html cook_method stores and serves unsanitized feed HTML verbatim, so a hostile or compromised feed yields stored XSS on the forum origin

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw` when `cook_method == :raw_html` (app/models/post.rb). New code paths set this cook_method for imported content: `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `raw: absolutize_urls(url, contents)` and `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and `Jobs::PollFeed` passes `i.content` from the feed directly into `TopicEmbed.import` after only `CGI.unescapeHTML` and `.scrub` (no HTML sanitization). Because the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline is explicitly skipped, any malicious HTML/attributes from a hostile or compromised feed (or remote page via `import_remote`) can be stored as `raw`/`cooked` and later rendered verbatim (e.g., embed view uses `<%= raw post.cooked %>`), creating a stored XSS risk on the Discourse origin.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:12 — request.referer` is interpolated unescaped into a JS string literal and used as postMessage targetOrigin, allowing injection via a crafted Referer
app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:17 — Origin check uses `indexOf(e.origin) === -1`, a substring test that accepts any origin that happens to be a substring of discourseUrl
app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15 — Unauthenticated requests enqueue a RetrieveTopic job for any embed_url before any host validation, letting an attacker flood the job queue

adjudication.rationale: EmbedController has a before_filter `ensure_embeddable`, but that filter only validates the *request.referer* host against `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`; it does not validate the `embed_url` param’s host before enqueuing. In `best`, when no TopicEmbed exists it unconditionally does `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)`. The job’s `TopicRetriever` will later reject invalid `embed_url` hosts (`invalid_host?`), but the Sidekiq job is already queued. Since the route is a simple GET (`get 'embed/best'`) with no authentication requirement and no throttling here, an attacker can send many requests (and can spoof the Referer header to pass `ensure_embeddable`) to flood the job queue with no-op RetrieveTopic jobs for arbitrary `embed_url` values.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26 — The sole access gate is a trivially spoofable Referer header, and specs stub it so the gate looks verified

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` the only request-origin check is `URI(request.referer || '').host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, and access is denied solely based on that header. The `Referer` header is client-controlled and can be omitted or spoofed by non-browser clients (e.g., curl), so it’s not a strong access-control mechanism. The specs do stub `request.referer` to exercise the “success” path, but that doesn’t change the underlying issue that the protection relies on a spoofable header.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — Calling PollFeed inline bypasses its `retry: false`, so feed exceptions propagate into RetrieveTopic and are retried, re-polling the entire feed each time

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb `perform_retrieve` calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` synchronously (inline). The `sidekiq_options retry: false` in app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb only affects Sidekiq when the job is enqueued/run by Sidekiq, not when `execute` is invoked directly. As a result, any exception from `PollFeed#poll_feed` (e.g., `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` network errors or `SimpleRSS.parse` errors) will bubble up through `TopicRetriever#retrieve`. Since `TopicRetriever` is used by the `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` job (app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb) which does not disable retries, Sidekiq’s default retry behavior would retry `RetrieveTopic`, re-running `perform_retrieve` and re-polling the feed each retry attempt.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — Staff bypass the throttle entirely, so each staff page load triggers a full synchronous feed poll and remote fetch

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows staff can bypass the 60s throttle: `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` passes `no_throttle: user.try(:staff?)`, and `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` returns `false` when `@opts[:no_throttle]` is true. However, the finding’s main claim is not verifiable: embed page loads do **not** synchronously poll feeds/fetch remote content. `EmbedController#best` enqueues `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` and renders `loading`; the poll/feed fetch happens asynchronously inside the Sidekiq job. Also, even with no throttle, `perform_retrieve` bails out if the embed already exists (`TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?`), so it’s not true that “each staff page load” triggers a full poll/fetch unconditionally.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:79 — topic_id_for_embed requires an exact URL match while import stores the feed's link/id, so any normalization difference leaves the page reloading and re-enqueueing a job every 30s forever
app/models/topic_embed.rb:37 — content_sha1 is updated via update_column even when revise! returns false or the save failed, permanently suppressing retries of that changed content

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import’s update path, when content_sha1 has changed, it calls `revisor.revise!(...)` but ignores its return value and then unconditionally executes `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)`. Since `PostRevisor#revise!` can return `false` (e.g., `should_revise?` fails) and `update_post`’s `@post.save(...)` can also fail (it returns a boolean and is not checked), the embed’s `content_sha1` can be advanced even if the post content was not actually updated. That would prevent subsequent runs from attempting to apply the changed content because the stored sha now matches.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/post_revisor.rb:85 — @post.save(validate: ...)` return value is ignored, so a failed write is silently reported as a successful revision
spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb:40 — Update test asserts on the in-memory post without reloading, so a revision that never persisted still passes

adjudication.rationale: In `spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb` the “Supports updating the post” example calls `TopicEmbed.import(...)` a second time and immediately asserts on `post.cooked` from the returned ActiveRecord instance, without reloading from the database. Since `TopicEmbed.import` updates via `PostRevisor.new(post).revise!(...)` on an already-loaded `post` (`embed.post`), a failure to persist (e.g., `save` not happening / returning false / transaction rollback) could still leave the Ruby object mutated in memory and make `post.cooked` match, so the test would pass without proving the revision was actually saved.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:12 — Each guard test leaves the other settings at blank defaults, so the test passes even if the guard it claims to cover is deleted

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In Jobs::PollFeed#execute, poll_feed only runs when all three conditions are true: feed_polling_enabled?, feed_polling_url.present?, and embed_by_username.present?. In spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb, each “requires X” example stubs only one setting and leaves the others at their defaults from config/site_settings.yml (feed_polling_enabled: false, feed_polling_url: '', embed_by_username: ''). Because those defaults already make the combined condition false, the expectation `poll_feed` is never called would still pass even if the specific guard being tested were removed, so the tests don’t actually verify each individual guard.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:11 — Unique btree index on an unbounded embed_url string; a >2700-byte URL from a hostile feed raises on insert and kills the poll

adjudication.rationale: In the migration, `embed_url` is declared as `t.string :embed_url, null: false`, which in Rails creates a bounded `varchar(255)` (unless an explicit limit is changed, which it is not here). So it is not an “unbounded” string, and the claimed >2700-byte unique btree index failure is not supported by the diff. A very long URL would more plausibly fail due to the column length constraint (value too long for varchar(255)), not an index-on-unbounded-text issue as described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — contents <<` mutates the caller's string, so a retried or repeated import appends the "imported from" footer again

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the line `contents << "\n<hr>..."` appends to the same String object passed in as `contents`, which is a mutating operation in Ruby. This is directly verifiable from the diff. If the caller reuses the same String instance for a retry or multiple imports (e.g., calling `import` twice with the same `contents` variable/object), the footer will be appended again, changing the content and SHA1 unexpectedly. This side effect is a real correctness risk introduced by the code as written.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:13 — If the embedded topic is deleted TopicView.new raises, and perform_retrieve bails because the embed row still exists, permanently breaking that embed

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best the code trusts TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url) and immediately does `TopicView.new(topic_id, ...)` when a `topic_id` is returned. `topic_id_for_embed` is just a `pluck(:topic_id)` from `topic_embeds` and does not verify that the referenced Topic still exists. Separately, TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve immediately returns if any TopicEmbed row exists for the URL (`return if TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?`). The diff adds TopicEmbed without any shown cleanup/cascade behavior on Topic/Post deletion, and the DB has no foreign keys, so an orphaned topic_embeds row is possible. In that situation: (1) controller will raise when building TopicView for a non-existent topic, and (2) retrieval will be prevented because the embed row exists, so the embed can’t self-heal. This is a concrete correctness risk implied by the added logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:64 — Protocol-relative URLs (`//evil.com`) start with '/' and are rewritten into local paths, silently corrupting feed links

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, any `href`/`src` that `start_with?('/')` is rewritten as `"#{prefix}/#{href.sub(/^\/+/, '')}"`. Protocol-relative URLs like `//evil.com/x` also start with `/`, so they get rewritten to something like `http:///evil.com/x`, corrupting the intended external link. This behavior is directly verifiable from the diff and affects both `` and `` rewriting.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:4 — New embed.css/embed.js assets are not added to any precompile list, so the embed layout fails in production

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new standalone assets `app/assets/stylesheets/embed.css.scss` and `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, and the new layout references `stylesheet_link_tag 'embed'`. However, the diff does not show any existing asset pipeline configuration (e.g., `config/initializers/assets.rb` or `config/application.rb`) that determines what gets precompiled in production. Without seeing that configuration, it’s not verifiable from this diff alone that these assets are missing from the precompile list or that production will fail to serve them—some apps precompile all assets or include additional manifests. So the finding depends on repo context not present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:3 — force: true` makes the migration silently drop an existing topic_embeds table and its data on re-run

adjudication.rationale: The migration explicitly calls `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true`, which in Rails will issue a DROP TABLE (if the table already exists) before creating it. So if this migration is applied in an environment where `topic_embeds` already exists but the migration hasn’t been recorded as run (or the migration is otherwise re-applied), it can delete existing data. This behavior is directly implied by `force: true` and is present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/best.html.erb:6 — Stray `<%- end if %>` is invalid ERB and will raise for every third-party consumer of embed/best.
matched_golden_ids: The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both the golden comment and the candidate issue point out that the ERB/Ruby block is incorrectly closed with `end if`, which is invalid and will raise during rendering; it should be closed with just `end`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26 — Access to the public embed endpoint is gated solely on the Referer header, so any caller whose browser/proxy strips Referer gets a hard InvalidAccess instead of the embed.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, access is enforced by comparing `URI(request.referer || '').host` to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` and raising `Discourse::InvalidAccess` when they differ. If the `Referer` header is missing/stripped, `request.referer` is nil, `URI('')` yields a nil host, and the comparison fails, causing an exception. So the embed endpoint will hard-fail for requests without a Referer, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:17 — The postMessage contract validates sender origin with a substring `indexOf` check rather than an equality check, accepting messages from unrelated origins.
matched_golden_ids: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same security flaw: validating postMessage sender origin using a substring/indexOf check is bypassable (e.g., malicious domains containing the allowed origin) and should use strict origin equality/whitelisting.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:130 — cook` returns raw unsanitized HTML for raw_html posts, silently changing the guarantee every existing consumer of `cooked` (serializers, digests, feeds, search) relied on.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff changes `Post#cook` to immediately `return raw` when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (app/models/post.rb). This bypasses the normal cooking/rendering pipeline (`post_analyzer.cook` + plugin filter) that existing `cooked` consumers rely on for processed/sanitized HTML. The new RSS/remote import path explicitly sets `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (app/models/topic_embed.rb via PostCreator) using HTML content pulled from feeds/remote pages, and no sanitization is applied before storing/serving it. As a result, `post.cooked` can now contain unsanitized HTML for these posts, which is a concrete behavior change and potential XSS risk for any place that renders/uses `cooked`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:131 — The raw_html early return skips `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)`, breaking that published plugin hook for a whole class of posts.

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/post.rb, Post#cook now immediately returns `raw` when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. This bypasses the existing call to `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, self, ...)`, meaning the `:after_post_cook` plugin hook will not run for any posts marked `raw_html` (e.g., RSS-imported posts created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` in TopicEmbed.import). This is directly verifiable from the diff and can break plugins relying on that hook to post-process cooked content.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:19 — discourse_expires_in 1.minute` caches a response that varies by Referer and current_user without any Vary header, so shared caches can serve one caller's embed/loading page to another.
config/routes.rb:245 — New externally consumed `embed/best` route is added with no version or namespace and no format constraint, freezing an unversioned public URL contract.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add a new top-level GET route `get 'embed/best' => 'embed#best'`, and the new `embed.js` script explicitly consumes that path, so exposing an external URL is intentional. However, the claim that this is a “problem” because it lacks versioning/namespace or a format constraint is an architectural preference rather than a verifiable defect: Rails apps commonly add unversioned HTML routes, and nothing in the diff shows a requirement for API-style versioning or that multiple formats would cause incorrect behavior. There’s no demonstrated bug, security issue, or correctness failure arising from the lack of version/format constraints in this route.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26 — Only one exact `embeddable_host` is supported (no port/scheme/www/multi-host), so any other subdomain of an existing caller silently breaks.

adjudication.rationale: The diff intentionally introduces a single SiteSetting.embeddable_host and enforces an exact host match via `URI(request.referer).host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host` in `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` (and similarly in `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?`). This does mean subdomains like `www.` or other hosts are rejected, but that aligns with the setting being a singular “Host that can embed…” and is not clearly a defect. Also, failure is not “silent”: it raises `Discourse::InvalidAccess`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:9 — params.require(:embed_url)` raises ParameterMissing, surfacing as a 500 to third-party callers instead of a documented 400 response.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce `embed_url = params.require(:embed_url)` in `EmbedController#best`, which will raise `ActionController::ParameterMissing` when the param is absent. However, in Rails (notably Rails 4, consistent with `Gemfile_rails4.lock`), `ParameterMissing` is treated as a client error and is typically rendered as a 400 Bad Request by the framework/middleware rather than surfacing as an unhandled 500. The added controller spec (`it "is 404 without an embed_url"`) exercises the missing-param case and only asserts “not success”, consistent with a handled 4xx response. The claim that it becomes a 500 is not verifiable from the diff and is likely incorrect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:28 — X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL` is not a valid header value; the framing contract depends on browsers ignoring it and is defeated by any proxy/global DENY.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` which sets `response.headers['X-Frame-Options'] = "ALLOWALL"`. `X-Frame-Options` only supports standard values like `DENY`, `SAMEORIGIN`, and (deprecated) `ALLOW-FROM <uri>`; `ALLOWALL` is not a valid value and many browsers will ignore it. That makes the intended behavior (allow embedding in an iframe) unreliable and can be overridden/negated by other layers that set a valid X-Frame-Options value (e.g., middleware/proxies setting DENY/SAMEORIGIN). This is a concrete defect in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:11 — postMessage targetOrigin is the full referer URL (and is unescaped/possibly blank), an ill-specified origin that can throw and silently disable iframe resizing.
matched_golden_ids: postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out that `postMessage` is using the full referrer URL as `targetOrigin` instead of a proper origin (scheme+host+port), which can cause the message to be dropped and break iframe resizing. The candidate adds extra notes (unescaped/blank), but the core issue matches.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:65 — protocol-relative URLs ("//host/path") start with '/' and are rewritten to prefix + host/path, corrupting the link

The code then does `href.sub(/^\/+/, '')`, which strips both leading slashes, producing `cdn.example.com/x`, and prefixes it with `prefix` (the embed_url’s scheme+host), resulting in a corrupted URL like `http://origin-host/cdn.example.com/x` instead of preserving `//cdn.example.com/x`. adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:52 — doc.title/doc.content can be nil when readability fails to parse, propagating nil into import and blowing up on contents <<

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:33 — i.id may be nil or a non-URL guid, so import silently returns nil and the item is skipped forever

If `i.id` is nil or a non-URL GUID (common in RSS/Atom), `url` will be nil or non-http(s). `TopicEmbed.import` immediately returns nil unless `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, so the item will not be imported and there is no logging/error handling here. adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 — open() failures (network/404) propagate uncaught with retry disabled, silently killing the scheduled poll

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb the job does `rss = SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` with no exception handling. `open-uri` can raise (e.g., OpenURI::HTTPError for 404/500, SocketError, Timeout::Error), and `SimpleRSS.parse` can also raise on malformed feeds. Since the job sets `sidekiq_options retry: false`, any such transient failure will cause the scheduled run to error out with no Sidekiq retry of that execution, preventing feed processing for that run.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:27 — setnx followed by a separate expire is not atomic; a crash between them leaves the throttle key with no TTL, blocking that embed_url forever

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, the code throttles by doing `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and then, only if that succeeds, `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. These are two separate Redis commands with no transaction/Lua/SET NX EX to make them atomic. If the process crashes or is killed after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` runs, the key will be left without a TTL. On subsequent calls, `setnx` will fail and the method returns `true` (throttled) forever for that embed_url, effectively blocking retrieval permanently. This is a real correctness defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:15 — URI() can raise other errors (e.g. URI::BadURIError/ArgumentError) that are not rescued, so a malformed embed_url crashes the job

Additionally, in the paths introduced here (EmbedController `params.require(:embed_url)` and Jobs::RetrieveTopic’s presence check), `embed_url` is expected to be a present string; there’s no evidence in the diff that `URI()` will raise an unrescued `ArgumentError` for a malformed *string* URL beyond InvalidURIError. adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:3 — create_table with force: true silently drops an existing topic_embeds table and its data if the migration is re-run

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3 — Adding `cook_method` with `null: false, default: 1` rewrites the whole posts table under an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on old PostgreSQL, causing extended downtime on large forums.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:6 — embed_url` is an unbounded varchar under a btree unique index; URLs over the ~2704-byte index limit will fail the insert at the DB level.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — Synchronously runs the entire hourly PollFeed import inline on every embed cache-miss, re-parsing and re-importing the whole feed per request

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb, perform_retrieve calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true. `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` parses the configured feed URL and iterates `rss.items.each`, calling `TopicEmbed.import` for every item. This is executed synchronously inside the retrieval path for an individual embed URL cache-miss (before falling back to `fetch_http`), meaning a single embed miss can trigger a full feed parse/import pass. While the controller enqueues a background job (so not strictly inline in the HTTP request thread), the code does rerun the whole feed import on each cache-miss retrieval attempt, which is the core concern of the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — open(url).read pulls an arbitrary remote document fully into memory with no size cap, read timeout, or redirect limit

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, the code does `open(url).read` and passes the full string into `Readability::Document.new(...)`. The diff shows no explicit content-length limit, streaming, or configured open/read timeouts in that call, so a large/slow response can be read fully into memory and tie up the worker. There is also no explicit redirect limit in this code path (it relies on open-uri defaults). While the host is constrained elsewhere (`TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` compares against `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`), the path/document is still user-controlled within that host and can be arbitrarily large, so the underlying risk described is present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 — SimpleRSS.parse open(feed_url) fetches and materializes the whole feed in memory with no timeout or size limit

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb the job does `rss = SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`. This uses open-uri with no explicit `open_timeout`, `read_timeout`, redirect limits, or maximum download size, so the scheduled Sidekiq job can block for a long time on a slow/unresponsive server and may download an arbitrarily large feed into memory for parsing. Those protections are not present anywhere in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:31 — Iterates every feed item unbounded, doing a SELECT plus PostCreator/PostRevisor per item (N+1 writes) with no batching or max-item cap

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, `poll_feed` does `rss.items.each do |i|` with no limit/cap or batching. For each item it calls `TopicEmbed.import`, which performs at least one DB lookup (`TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first`) and may then do a transaction with `PostCreator`/`PostRevisor` writes. That is a per-item SELECT plus potentially multiple writes, repeated for every feed entry, making the job unbounded in work proportional to feed size and effectively N+1 DB operations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/best.html.erb:16 — post.user is dereferenced per post in the loop, an N+1 user query unless TopicView eager-loads users

As stated, it depends on code outside the diff and is therefore speculative.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:9 — Loading page hard-reloads every 30s forever, so each pending embed generates unbounded repeat requests and retrieve_topic job enqueues

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when no `topic_id` is found it always does `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ... embed_url: embed_url)` and renders `loading`. The loading template (`app/views/embed/loading.html.erb`) runs `document.location.reload()` every 30 seconds with no stop condition, which will re-request `/embed/best?embed_url=...` indefinitely until the embed exists. That means repeated HTTP requests and repeated `retrieve_topic` job enqueues for the same pending embed. Although `TopicRetriever` later throttles actual retrieval work via Redis, the controller still enqueues a new job on every reload, so the “unbounded repeat requests and job enqueues” described is a real behavior in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:19 — discourse_expires_in 1.minute is very short for an iframe hit by every blog page view, giving little cache relief on TopicView cost

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `EmbedController#best` calling `discourse_expires_in 1.minute`, but nothing in the change makes that value objectively incorrect or broken. The claim that it gives “little cache relief” is speculative and not a verifiable defect introduced by the diff (no evidence of unacceptable TopicView cost, missing caching headers, or requirements for longer caching).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15 — Job is enqueued per request before the redis throttle is consulted, so bursts flood the sidekiq queue with duplicate retrieve_topic jobs

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when no `topic_id` exists it unconditionally does `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)` on every request (line ~15 in the new controller). The Redis throttling (`retrieved_recently?` using `$redis.setnx`/`expire`) exists only inside `TopicRetriever#retrieve`, which is invoked later by the Sidekiq job (`Jobs::RetrieveTopic`). Therefore, a burst of web requests can enqueue many duplicate `retrieve_topic` jobs before any throttle check runs, potentially flooding the Sidekiq queue even though most jobs will no-op when executed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:79 — pluck(:topic_id).first materializes all matching rows instead of using limit(1)

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed`, the query filters by `embed_url`, and the migration adds a **unique index** on `topic_embeds.embed_url`, so there can be at most one matching row. `pluck(:topic_id).first` will therefore return an array of 0 or 1 elements in normal operation, not “materialize all matching rows” in any meaningful way. This is at most a micro-optimization/style suggestion (could use `limit(1)`/`pick`), not a real defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:61 — absolutize_urls builds a full Nokogiri DOM and re-serializes the whole article body on every import/update

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, which parses `contents` via `Nokogiri::HTML.fragment(contents)` and then calls `fragment.to_html`, so it does parse and re-serialize the whole HTML string on each import/update where `absolutize_urls` is used. However, this is an inherent/intentional implementation choice to safely rewrite relative `href`/`src` attributes and is not a clear defect (bug/security/correctness issue) introduced by the diff—it's a performance/optimization observation without evidence of causing a real problem.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 — open-uri fetch of the feed URL has no open/read timeout, so a slow or hung remote feed can block a Sidekiq worker indefinitely

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb the feed is fetched via `rss = SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` (with `require 'open-uri'`) and no `:open_timeout` / `:read_timeout` options are provided. That means the job relies on open-uri/Net::HTTP defaults and does not enforce bounded network time; a slow/hung feed endpoint can tie up the scheduled Sidekiq worker for an unbounded/very long period (e.g., slow trickle responses), which is a real operational correctness issue introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — import_remote calls open(url) with no timeout and no rescue, so a hung or erroring remote site blocks/kills the RetrieveTopic job

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/topic_embed.rb import_remote does `open(url).read` (via open-uri) with no explicit open/read timeouts passed and no exception handling around the network fetch. This method is invoked from TopicRetriever#fetch_http, which is called by the RetrieveTopic background job. As written, slow/hung remote responses can tie up the Sidekiq worker for an extended period, and network errors (timeouts, DNS, connection failures) will raise and fail the job since nothing rescues them here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:21 — wrapping PostCreator in an outer Topic.transaction makes PostCreator's inner ActiveRecord::Rollback a no-op, so spam-rejected/partial posts get committed instead of rolled back

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `TopicEmbed.import` wrapping a `PostCreator#create` call in `Topic.transaction`, but it does not show `PostCreator` raising/rescuing `ActiveRecord::Rollback` (the claim depends on unseen code). Also, in Rails, an `ActiveRecord::Rollback` raised inside a nested transaction is not made a “no-op” by an outer transaction; if anything, without `requires_new` it rolls back the whole transaction. From the diff alone, there’s no verifiable path where spam-rejected/partial posts would be committed due to this outer transaction.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:12 — retry: false combined with no rescue means any transient network or parse error silently discards the entire hourly poll with no alerting

adjudication.rationale: In the new `Jobs::PollFeed` scheduled job, `sidekiq_options retry: false` is indeed set and the code does not rescue around `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` / `SimpleRSS.parse`, so an exception would fail that run without Sidekiq retries. However, the claim that the failure is “silently discarded … with no alerting” is not verifiable from the diff: Sidekiq will still surface/log job exceptions by default, and the job will run again on the next hourly schedule. This is more of a resilience/design preference than a clear defect proven by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:31 — no per-item error handling: one malformed feed item aborts the loop and all remaining items are never imported

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, rss.items.each processes items without any per-item rescue. The code assumes i.content is present and responds to scrub (content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)); if a feed item has nil/invalid content (or other unexpected structure), this will raise (e.g., NoMethodError) and abort the entire job, preventing remaining items from being imported. Nothing in the loop handles exceptions per item, so the finding is directly supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 — i.content is assumed non-nil (many RSS feeds only supply description), so nil.scrub raises NoMethodError and kills the whole poll

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, poll_feed does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. `i` is an item from `SimpleRSS.parse`, and RSS/Atom items do not always have a `content` field (many provide `description`/`summary` instead). If `i.content` is nil, calling `.scrub` will raise `NoMethodError`, aborting the job and preventing the rest of the feed from being processed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:20 — feed_key (Last-Modified/ETag cache key) is computed but never used, so every hourly run refetches and reprocesses the full feed

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, the method `feed_key` is defined (computing a SHA1-based key from `SiteSetting.feed_polling_url`) but is never referenced anywhere in the job. The `poll_feed` method always does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and then iterates `rss.items` on every run, with no use of `feed_key` (or any Redis/DB state) to avoid refetching/reprocessing unchanged feeds. While `TopicEmbed.import` may no-op on unchanged items via `content_sha1`, the feed itself is still always fetched and fully parsed each time.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — RetrieveTopic synchronously runs the entire PollFeed job inline, so a user request can tie up a worker on an unbounded full-feed fetch

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In lib/topic_retriever.rb, perform_retrieve calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true. `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` performs a network fetch (`SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`) and then iterates all `rss.items` importing each one. TopicRetriever is invoked from the enqueued `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` (app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb), which is triggered by EmbedController when an embed is missing. This means a single embed request can cause a sidekiq worker to synchronously do a potentially long/unbounded full-feed fetch+import, tying up the worker and amplifying load (especially if many embeds are requested).

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:27 — setnx followed by a separate expire is not atomic; a crash between them leaves the throttle key with no TTL, permanently blocking retrieval of that embed_url

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, the throttle key is created with `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and only then given a TTL via a separate `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. If the process crashes or is killed after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` runs, the key will exist without an expiration. Subsequent calls will see `setnx` fail and treat it as “retrieved recently” indefinitely, permanently blocking retrieval for that embed_url (until manual Redis cleanup).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:10 — raising Discourse::InvalidParameters for a permanently bad argument causes Sidekiq to retry the job 25 times with backoff instead of failing fast

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb`, `execute` raises `Discourse::InvalidParameters.new(:embed_url)` when `args[:embed_url]` is missing. The job does not declare `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so under Sidekiq’s default behavior an exception will trigger automatic retries (commonly 25). Since a missing `embed_url` is a non-transient/parameter error, retrying would be wasted work and log noise rather than “fail fast”. This behavior is directly implied by the code in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:37 — content_sha1 is updated unconditionally even when revisor.revise! returns false, so a failed revision is recorded as applied and never retried

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import’s update path, when `content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1`, the code calls `revisor.revise!(...)` but ignores its return value and then unconditionally executes `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)`. Since `PostRevisor#revise!` can return `false` (it explicitly does so when `should_revise?` is false, and `save` can also fail), this can record the new SHA1 even if the post revision did not actually apply, preventing future retries because subsequent imports will see matching SHA1 and skip revising.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:32 — embed.post can be nil (post deleted/purged) and is passed straight to PostRevisor.new, raising inside the job

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, when an existing TopicEmbed is found, it does `post = embed.post` and, if the content hash changed, immediately calls `PostRevisor.new(post)` (lines ~32-38 in the new file). `embed.post` can be `nil` if the referenced post record has been deleted (there is no foreign key constraint shown, and the association will return nil if the row is missing). In that case, `PostRevisor.new(nil)` will raise (or later calls will), causing the feed/import job path to error. There is no nil-guard or recovery behavior in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:15 — concurrent PollFeed/RetrieveTopic runs can both see a blank embed and race on the unique embed_url index, raising an unhandled RecordNotUnique

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import`, it does `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and if blank proceeds to `TopicEmbed.create!(..., embed_url: url, ...)` inside a transaction. The migration adds a unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url`. With two concurrent callers (e.g., `Jobs::PollFeed` and `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` / `TopicRetriever.fetch_http`) importing the same URL, both can observe no existing row and then race to `create!`; the loser will raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`. There is no rescue/handling in `TopicEmbed.import` (or callers), so this can bubble up and fail the job/request.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:24 — PostCreator returning a post with errors (nil id) or nil is not checked or logged, so import fails silently or raises a NOT NULL violation
app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — contents is mutated in place with << so a retried or re-imported item accumulates duplicate "imported from" footers and a changed sha1
app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15 — every uncached embed request enqueues a RetrieveTopic job with no dedup at enqueue time, allowing job flooding from repeated page loads

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, when TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url) returns nil, the code unconditionally calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: ..., embed_url: embed_url)` and renders `loading`. There is no guard or deduplication at enqueue time (no redis key check, no unique job, no existence check). Although TopicRetriever has a redis-based throttle in `retrieved_recently?`, that throttle runs during job execution, not before jobs are placed onto the queue, so repeated page loads can enqueue many redundant RetrieveTopic jobs and flood the job queue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:11 — hourly recurrence with no distributed lock or run timeout allows overlapping poll runs to import the same feed items concurrently
app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:11 — Attacker-controlled `request.referer` is interpolated unescaped into an inline JS string literal, allowing script injection (XSS) on the embed page.
matched_golden_ids: An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same XSS vulnerability: attacker-controlled `request.referer` is inserted into inline JavaScript without escaping, enabling script injection.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:133 — New `raw_html` cook method returns `raw` verbatim, bypassing Discourse's sanitizing cook pipeline so imported HTML (scripts, event handlers) is stored and rendered as-is.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `Post.cook_methods` with `:raw_html` and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, explicitly bypassing the normal cooking pipeline (`post_analyzer.cook` + plugin filters), which is where Discourse would typically sanitize/normalize HTML. The new embed import path sets `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` in `TopicEmbed.import` when creating posts from RSS/remote content, and that content is not otherwise sanitized (it is only URL-absolutized via Nokogiri; tags/attributes like `<script>` or `on*` handlers are not stripped). The embed view then renders `raw post.cooked`, which for these posts equals the unmodified `raw`. This makes the finding (unsanitized imported HTML rendered as-is) a real, verifiable security issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:36 — RSS/Atom item content is passed to `TopicEmbed.import` with zero sanitization and stored as raw_html, giving any feed publisher stored XSS on the forum.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the job takes `i.content` from the feed, only applies `CGI.unescapeHTML` and `.scrub` (encoding cleanup, not HTML sanitization), then passes it to `TopicEmbed.import`. `TopicEmbed.import` creates a post via `PostCreator` with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `skip_validations: true`. `Post#cook` explicitly returns `raw` when `cook_method` is `:raw_html`, bypassing the normal cooking/rendering pipeline where sanitization would typically occur. The embed view renders `raw post.cooked`, so any HTML/JS from the feed content can be stored and output as-is, enabling stored XSS if the feed is attacker-controlled or compromised.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19 — raw post.cooked` renders post HTML unescaped, which combined with the raw_html cook method yields stored XSS in the embed iframe.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff introduces a `raw_html` cook method that makes `Post#cook` return `raw` directly (`return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`), explicitly bypassing the normal rendering/sanitization pipeline. `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` using HTML pulled from RSS/remote pages (`i.content` / `doc.content`) and appends additional HTML containing the interpolated URL. In `app/views/embed/best.html.erb`, the template renders `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, so for these imported posts `post.cooked` will effectively be unescaped, externally-sourced HTML. This is a verifiable stored XSS risk inside the embed iframe (scripts/unsafe attributes from the imported content would execute under the Discourse origin).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — Source `url` is interpolated into a single-quoted `<a href='...'>` attribute without escaping, permitting attribute-breakout HTML/JS injection.
app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — open(url)` (open-uri) fetches a user-influenced URL and follows redirects, so an embeddable_host page can redirect to internal/metadata endpoints (SSRF).

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` does `open(url).read` on `url` derived from the user-supplied `embed_url` (via `EmbedController#best` → `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` → `TopicRetriever` → `TopicEmbed.import_remote`). Although `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` restricts the *initial* URL host to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, `open-uri` will follow HTTP redirects by default. That means an attacker who controls content on the allowed embeddable host (or can influence its redirects) can cause the server to fetch arbitrary redirected targets (e.g., `http://169.254.169.254/` or internal RFC1918 hosts), which is a verifiable SSRF risk introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26 — Authorization gate relies solely on the `Referer` header, which is trivially forged, so it provides no real access control for the embed endpoint.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, access is granted if `URI(request.referer || '').host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host` (and otherwise it raises). This is the only authorization check for the `/embed/best` endpoint, but `Referer` is a client-supplied header that can be omitted or trivially forged by non-browser clients (e.g., curl) and is not a trustworthy authentication/authorization mechanism. Therefore the gate does not provide real access control as implemented in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:13 — Topic is rendered from `topic_id` looked up by embed_url without any Guardian/`can_see?` check, so a private or restricted-category topic linked to an embed is exposed to anonymous users.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, the code does look up a `topic_id` purely from `embed_url` and instantiates `TopicView.new(topic_id, current_user, {best: 5})` without an explicit `Guardian`/`can_see?` check in this controller. However, whether this exposes a private/restricted topic is not verifiable from the diff: Discourse commonly enforces topic visibility inside `TopicView`/Guardian, and the diff does not show those implementations. Additionally, the controller does not explicitly skip any authentication requirement (only `:check_xhr` and `:preload_json` are skipped), so anonymous access is also not established by the diff alone. Therefore the claim of exposure to anonymous users is speculative based on code outside the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:28 — Setting `X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL` (a non-standard, effectively no-op value) disables framing protection for this response, enabling clickjacking of authenticated forum content.
app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:19 — discourse_expires_in` caches a per-user response (TopicView built with `current_user`) allowing shared/proxy caches to serve one user's view to another.
app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:17 — Origin check uses `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1`, a substring match that accepts unintended origins instead of a strict origin comparison.

app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:11 — postMessage` targetOrigin is the full referer URL (including path/query) rather than an origin, leaking the parent page URL and weakening the intended origin restriction.

adjudication.rationale: In app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb the iframe sends `parent.postMessage(..., '<%= request.referer %>')`. The `targetOrigin` parameter must be an origin (scheme + host + optional port) or "*", not a full URL including path/query. Using the full referer URL can cause the browser to reject/throw on the call or prevent delivery because it won’t match `event.origin` semantics, undermining the intended origin restriction and potentially breaking resize messaging.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15 — Unauthenticated requests with arbitrary `embed_url` enqueue server-side fetch jobs with no rate limiting on the endpoint, enabling job-queue/outbound-request abuse.

adjudication.rationale: The new `EmbedController#best` enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)` whenever no existing `TopicEmbed` is found (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb). This action is reachable for anonymous users (specs call `TopicView.new(123, nil, ...)`), and there is no controller-side throttling before enqueueing. Although `TopicRetriever#retrieve` applies a Redis throttle, it runs inside the job after it has already been enqueued, so repeated requests can still flood the job queue (and by varying `embed_url` paths/queries under the allowed host, can trigger many distinct throttled keys and outbound fetch attempts). Thus the finding describes a real abuse vector introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:14 — Host check compares only `URI(url).host` and ignores the scheme, so non-HTTP schemes (e.g. file:/ftp:) can reach `open()` in the retrieval path.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` only compares `URI(@embed_url).host` to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` and does not restrict the scheme. If an attacker supplies an `embed_url` like `ftp://<embeddable_host>/...` (or other non-http(s) schemes that still have the same host), `invalid_host?` returns false and the retrieval path reaches `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, which does `open(url).read` without validating the scheme. Even though `TopicEmbed.import` later rejects non-`/^https?:\/\//` URLs, the `open()` call has already been made, enabling non-HTTP scheme fetch attempts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 — open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` uses Kernel#open on a settable string, which treats a leading `|` as a shell command and permits SSRF to internal hosts.
matched_golden_ids: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point to the PollFeed job calling `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` on an attacker-controlled/site-setting URL without validation, enabling the server to fetch arbitrary internal/external URLs (SSRF). The candidate adds the additional risk of `Kernel#open` interpreting a leading `|` as a shell command, but it still identifies the same core issue as the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/post_revisor.rb:85 — New `skip_validations` option lets callers persist posts bypassing all model validations, removing content/length/spam safeguards.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `PostRevisor#update_post` from unconditional `@post.save` to `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`, explicitly introducing a new `skip_validations` escape hatch that disables *all* ActiveRecord validations when set. This option is then exercised in the diff: `TopicEmbed.import` calls `revisor.revise!(user, ..., skip_validations: true, bypass_rate_limiter: true)`, meaning remotely imported/updated content can be persisted without model validation safeguards (e.g., length/presence/format/custom validation logic). This is a real behavioral/security-relevant change in the diff, not speculation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:40 — Test mocks TopicRetriever.new/retrieve but the controller enqueues Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic), so it asserts a collaboration that no longer exists and never covers the real enqueue path

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `EmbedController#best` enqueues a job when no embed exists: `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: ..., embed_url: embed_url)` and renders `loading`. It never instantiates `TopicRetriever` directly. However, `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb` (the test described in the finding) expects `TopicRetriever.new` to be called and `retriever.retrieve` to run during the controller action. That collaboration does not exist in the controller code shown, so the spec is asserting the wrong behavior and does not cover the actual enqueue path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:18 — "requires feed_polling_url" only stubs feed_polling_url nil while feed_polling_enabled? defaults to false, so the example passes vacuously and would still pass if the url guard were deleted

adjudication.rationale: In `Jobs::PollFeed#execute`, `poll_feed` only runs if `feed_polling_enabled?` is true AND `feed_polling_url.present?` AND `embed_by_username.present?`. The spec example "requires feed_polling_url" only stubs `SiteSetting.feed_polling_url` to `nil` and does not stub `feed_polling_enabled?`. The default for `feed_polling_enabled` is set to `false` in `config/site_settings.yml` in this diff, so the condition short-circuits on the first check and the example would still pass even if the `feed_polling_url.present?` guard were removed. Thus the test is vacuous and does not actually verify the URL requirement.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:24 — "requires embed_by_username" is likewise vacuous (feed polling disabled by default), asserting nothing about the embed_by_username guard

adjudication.rationale: In Jobs::PollFeed#execute, poll_feed is only called if all three guards are true: feed_polling_enabled?, feed_polling_url.present?, and embed_by_username.present?. In spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb, the "requires embed_by_username" example only stubs SiteSetting.embed_by_username to nil and asserts poll_feed is never called, but it does not stub feed_polling_enabled? to true or feed_polling_url to a present value. Given the defaults added in config/site_settings.yml (feed_polling_enabled: false, feed_polling_url: ''), the condition will be false regardless of embed_by_username, so the test would still pass even if the embed_by_username check were removed. That makes the test effectively vacuous and not actually verifying the intended guard.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb:34 — absolutize_urls edge cases untested: non-default port prefix, protocol-relative/absolute hrefs, and img/a tags with blank src/href

adjudication.rationale: The proposed finding is about missing test coverage (edge cases not exercised) rather than a verifiable defect introduced by the diff. In spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb the test only asserts conversion of simple root-relative URLs; it’s true it doesn’t cover non-default ports or protocol-relative URLs, but that’s not itself a bug/security/correctness issue demonstrated by the diff—just an observation about additional tests that could be added.
